research_question: Can RAKL distinguish a merely navigable chain of individually valid analogies from an end-to-end transfer-composable bridge without silently changing the invariant, role semantics, question/QoI, regime, approximation budget, evidence ancestry, or authority across hops?
frozen_principles: BRIDGE_TO denotes navigation and never automatic endpoint equivalence
each hop requires its own valid typed similarity witness
adjacent hops must share the same intermediate object identity
end-to-end transfer requires a declared invariant preserved on every hop
a carried invariant explicitly listed NOT_PRESERVED on any hop invalidates its end-to-end composition
shared-node role semantics must be compatible across adjacent hops
question/QoI must remain fixed in v1 unless a future separately benchmarked transition contract is added
end-to-end transfer requires non-empty intersection of validity regimes across all hops
approximation/error accumulation must be explicit and predeclared
shared evidence ancestry cannot be counted as independent multi-hop corroboration
a composable path yields a transfer hypothesis only; it never creates target authority or an inferred endpoint relation without a separately registered composition rule
hidden answer exposure and post-hoc path/invariant selection invalidate the trial

worlds.description: A->B and B->C are valid witnesses under one QoI, preserve the same declared invariant, share compatible B roles, have overlapping regimes and explicit nonnegative error bounds.
A->B preserves feedback while B->C preserves threshold structure, with no invariant carried across all hops.
First hop ends at B1 while second hop starts at B2 despite surface naming similarity.
Both hops touch B but the source role used by the second hop is incompatible with the target role delivered by the first.
A->B concerns stability while B->C concerns throughput, with no registered QoI-transition contract.
Each pair is locally valid but no single regime is valid across the complete A->B->C path.
The path claims conservation as an end-to-end invariant but one hop lists conservation in NOT_PRESERVED.
The path declares an invariant that is neither preserved nor explicitly broken on one hop.
All structural handoffs pass but one hop lacks an approximation/error bound needed by the claimed end-to-end transfer.
Per-hop approximation bounds are valid but their conservative accumulated upper bound exceeds the frozen path tolerance.
A hop reports a negative approximation error or malformed error semantics.
All hops compose structurally but their evidence descends from one shared source lineage.
The path constructor sees the benchmark-designated successful endpoint before bridge selection.
The carried invariant or intermediate path is selected after inspecting endpoint outcomes.
Only one similarity witness is supplied.
A->B is observationally equivalent and B->C is mathematically isomorphic; the system attempts to mint SAME_MECHANISM for A->C.
The structural path is valid and composable, but the transferred hypothesis fails a frozen target-domain test.
The structural path is valid and composable and the frozen target test passes.

acceptance_rule.support_layer: All known-answer, hostile and cannot-check worlds must match the frozen expected state; no endpoint relation or target authority may be minted by path composition.
acceptance_rule.active_workflow: Not authorized by this benchmark alone. A Class B activation would additionally require a matched real scientific bridge benchmark with at least one registered meta-QoI improvement and no blocking regression.

falsifier: If explicit path certificates do not improve composition-error detection or transfer precision over validating pairwise hops independently on a matched real benchmark, keep BRIDGE_TO as simple navigation and do not add richer active composition machinery.
